name: Seerr
description: A request desk in front of a media server: people search for a film or a series, ask for it, and the owner approves. One container with its own SQLite database; it is the continuation of Overseerr and Jellyseerr, which merged under this name.

access.note: Seerr has no account of its own. The first visitor lands on /setup, points it at a Jellyfin, Plex or Emby server that already exists, and signs in with an account from that server — which then becomes the owner here. Without such a server the wizard cannot be finished, so have one ready before deploying, and open the address yourself first.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: Optional; the address other people open. Seerr keeps its own "Application URL" — the one it puts in notification emails — in Settings rather than in the environment, so set it there too once you are signed in.

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The web interface and the request API

volumes.name: config
volumes.purpose: settings.json, the SQLite database of users and requests, and the logs

update.notes: Seerr migrates its database on start. It runs strictly as an unprivileged user, so the config volume must be writable by it — a fresh named volume is.
